definitions.explanation: Archaic and literary first-person pronoun, surviving in modern Japanese almost exclusively in fixed idioms. Refers to the self, especially one's own desires or will.

examples.japanese: {我|わ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れて→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧⟦{歌|うた}った→歌う：00684_utau⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{我|わ}を{張|は}って、⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}かない→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: He always insists on his own way and won't listen to other people's opinions.

notes:
Archaic first-person pronoun preserved in a small set of fixed expressions. Not used productively in modern Japanese — learners encounter it only in these idioms or in formal/literary writing.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {我|わ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}す→通す：02300_toosu⟧: to have one's way; to insist on one's own view
- {我|わ}を{張|は}る: to be stubborn; to refuse to yield
- {我|わ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れる→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧: to forget oneself; to lose oneself (in an activity or emotion)
- {我|わ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{返|かえ}る→返る：29164_kaeru⟧: to come to one's senses

PRONUNCIATION:
The same kanji {我} is also read われ (similarly archaic/literary, used as a stand-alone pronoun) and ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ (in compounds like {我儘|わがまま} selfish). The reading わ specifically appears in the idioms above.
